name: layout-composition-resolution
body: Layout composition resolution: `{{ template "<name>" . }}` is the standard Go html/template action over the library's layout namespace, not one of the six layout helpers (template-language). Its name is the library layout's file path — the layer root joined with the layout's path within its layer: `<layer root>/slides/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl` for a slide layout and `<layer root>/sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl` for a section layout. That path is the name the loader builds (`path.Join(root, layoutRel)`, loadlibrary.go) and the name render registers each layout under (`layoutName` / `namespaceForLayer`, render.go); it is the layout's path, not the template name. The namespace holds the layout texts of the layer it is built for, keyed by that name and parsed with the executing template's own owning layer's function set (`namespaceForLayer` at render time, `exampleLayoutNamespace` at the load-time example check): at render time it is the merged library's layout set, and at the load-time example check the external layer's namespace holds only that layer's own layouts while the local layer's namespace holds the merged set (example-layout-composition). A layout thus invokes another layout its namespace carries, a slide layout or a section layout alike, by that path name: a local-layer layout invokes an external-layer layout by the target's own root-qualified path name (for example `{{ template "<external root>/sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl" . }}`), and an external-layer layout's `{{ template }}` call naming a local-layer layout is a templates error at the external layer's own load. A `{{ template }}`-invoked layout executes in the invoking template's own namespace, so its `media` helper binds to the invoking template's own owning layer; a `section` helper call is the composition that executes a target under the target's own owning layer (library-layer-references).
